citations.narrative:
Multiple animal housing areas were found in structural disrepair, creating non-compliant conditions that compromise
animal safety. In the outdoor otter enclosure the asphalt floor is deteriorating, a section of the asphalt floor measuring
approximately 9 inches by 13 inches is missing, leaving jagged edges and a defect roughly 2 to 3 inches deep that
extends into the underlying substrate. This deteriorating flooring poses physical risks to the animals, including trauma
from sharp surfaces, potential injury from sharp exposed metal objects, and foreign body ingestion hazard from
uncovered debris. Furthermore, the artificial turf lining both the outdoor otter and outdoor capybara enclosures exhibits
advanced wear, featuring frayed perimeter edges, chewed sections, and noticeable tears. This degraded, unraveled fabric
creates a risk of foreign body ingestion and subsequent gastrointestinal obstruction. The facility must ensure that all
housing facilities and enclosure elements be maintained in good repair to protect the animals from injury, safeguard their
health, and prevent escape.

Numerous flies were observed throughout the facility, including but not limited to: the body of a convalescing wallaby,
exposed body surfaces of other resident animals, food preparation areas, and inside a number of other animal enclosure
surfaces including the open food and water receptacles. According to the licensee, the flies originate from an open
outdoor dumpster containing animal waste and garbage, entering the facility through an open garage door. While the
licensee stated that the current pest control program utilizes regularly refreshed fly strips, the program is ineffective. This
ongoing infestation poses a risk to the health and well-being of the animals, as flies can spread disease, contaminate feed
and water, and cause distress. To address these deficiencies, the licensee must establish, implement, and maintain a
safe and effective insect control program.
Correction to be completed by August 15, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
